title: How to Style a Royal Blue Anarkali 3 Ways (Wedding to Party)
excerpt: Three ways to style one royal blue georgette Anarkali: classic festive, modern minimal and winter daytime, with jewellery, hair and shoe tips.
body:
You can style a royal blue Anarkali three ways: classic festive with gold jhumkas and the dupatta draped on both shoulders, modern minimal with silver jewellery and the dupatta on one side, or winter daytime with a long coat, juttis and soft makeup. One outfit, three moods, and enough variety to wear it to a wedding, a party and a family lunch.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. Our Anarkalis are stitched in our own Jaipur unit.*

**Quick answer**

- Look 1, classic festive: gold jhumkas, dupatta on both shoulders, bun with flowers
- Look 2, modern minimal: silver or diamond-look studs, dupatta on one shoulder, sleek hair
- Look 3, winter daytime: long camel coat, juttis, loose waves and light makeup
- Royal blue suits gold, silver and pearls equally well
- Swap only accessories and hair to change the whole look

## Why is royal blue such a versatile Anarkali colour?

Royal blue is rich enough for an evening wedding and calm enough for a day event. It flatters most skin tones, from fair to deep, and it holds its colour under every kind of light: daylight, warm indoor bulbs and stage lights at a sangeet.

The [royal blue georgette Anarkali with handwork and gota lace dupatta](/products/royal-blue-georgette-anarkali-suit-gota-handwork-dupatta/) is a good base to restyle. Georgette drapes softly and moves well, and the gota lace on the dupatta adds just enough shine to dress it up.

If you want to know what to wear to a wedding in this colour, our post on [royal blue Anarkalis for wedding guests](/blog/what-to-wear-as-a-wedding-guest-royal-blue-anarkali/) covers it in detail. Here, we focus on restyling.

## How do the three looks compare?

| Look | Jewellery | Dupatta | Hair | Shoes | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Classic festive | Gold jhumkas, bangles | Both shoulders | Low bun with flowers | Embellished juttis | Wedding, Diwali, Eid |
| Modern minimal | Silver studs, cocktail ring | One shoulder, pinned | Sleek ponytail or bun | Strappy heels | Cocktail, New Year's Eve |
| Winter daytime | Pearl drops | Around the neck | Loose waves | Juttis, ankle boots outside | Family lunch, Christmas |

## How do I style it the classic festive way?

### Look 1: Classic festive

This is the full traditional look. Drape the gota lace dupatta over both shoulders so the border frames the outfit. Add gold jhumkas, a stack of bangles and a small bindi. Put your hair in a low bun and tuck in a few fresh flowers or a gajra.

This look is perfect for a wedding ceremony, a reception or Eid. It also photographs well in group pictures, because royal blue stands out next to the reds and pinks often worn at weddings. Our guide to [jewellery to wear with an Anarkali](/blog/jewellery-to-wear-with-an-anarkali/) explains how to match earrings to the neckline.

## How do I give it a modern minimal look?

### Look 2: Modern minimal

For a cocktail party or New Year's Eve, strip it back. Wear the dupatta over just one shoulder and pin it neatly at the back, or leave it off for a moment of photos. Swap gold for silver or diamond-look studs and a single cocktail ring. Wear your hair in a sleek ponytail or a high bun.

Add strappy heels and a metallic clutch, and the same [royal blue georgette Anarkali](/products/royal-blue-georgette-anarkali-suit-gota-handwork-dupatta/) suddenly feels like an evening gown. A bold berry or red lip completes the look.

## How do I wear it for a winter daytime event?

### Look 3: Winter daytime

For a Christmas lunch, a family visit or a daytime puja in cold weather, go soft and practical. Wrap the dupatta loosely around your neck like a scarf, or fold it over your arm. Wear pearl drop earrings and minimal makeup. Leave your hair in loose waves.

Outside, add a long camel or black coat and ankle boots, and change into juttis indoors. A wool shawl in grey or cream adds warmth and looks lovely against royal blue.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** Georgette has a slightly grainy surface that softens the light, so royal blue looks deep rather than shiny in photos. It also recovers well from creasing. Hang it in a steamy bathroom for ten minutes after travel, and most creases fall out.

If you love royal blue, you might like a second outfit in a related shade. The [purple bandhani chiffon Anarkali](/products/purple-bandhani-chiffon-anarkali-suit-set/) sits next to royal blue on the colour wheel and suits a mehendi or sangeet.

For a calmer day option, the [navy blue kota doria embroidered kurta set](/products/navy-blue-kota-doria-embroidered-kurta-pant-dupatta-set/) is lighter and easy to layer.

You can see more silhouettes in our [Anarkali suits](/anarkali-suits-online-usa-uk/) collection.

## Frequently asked questions

**What jewellery goes with a royal blue Anarkali?**
Gold, silver, pearls and kundan all work. Gold feels traditional, silver feels modern, and pearls look soft for daytime.

**What colour dupatta goes with a royal blue Anarkali?**
The matching gota lace dupatta is the easiest choice. For a contrast, try silver, soft pink or mustard.

**Can I wear a royal blue Anarkali to a day event?**
Yes. Keep the jewellery light, wear the dupatta around your neck and choose soft makeup and loose hair.

**How do I care for a georgette Anarkali?**
Dry cleaning is best for pieces with gota or handwork. Store it folded in a cotton bag and steam it to remove creases.
